title: Bury the dead
hookLine: Tobit risked his life to bury the dead
tomorrow: what did the stranger on the road do before he spoke?

lines: A DINNER THAT TAKES A TURN.
cards: Some family dinners take a turn. Someone mentions a will, or a plot at the cemetery, and the table goes quiet. The book of Tobit has a dinner like that.

It's a feast day, and Tobit sends his son out to bring back one of their people to share the meal. The son comes back with news instead: one of them is lying dead in the street. Tobit leaves the table without eating.
He carries the body home, hides it until the sun goes down, and buries it by night. He's done this before, and it nearly cost him his life.

teach.b: Why leave a feast for that? In Tobit's world, a king had his people killed and left unburied. Burying them said: they still count.
When the king found out, Tobit lost what he owned and fled. His neighbors mock him for starting again.
Near the end of the book, the angel Raphael tells him that when he prayed with tears and buried the dead, Raphael offered his prayer to the Lord.

teach.h: THE BURIALS WERE PART OF THE PRAYER.
teach.b: The burials were part of the prayer. The Church names burying the dead among the corporal works of mercy, and asks that the bodies of the dead be treated with respect and charity, in hope of the resurrection.
Now the question families face today, where Catholics land in two places.
The Church permits cremation, as long as it isn't chosen to deny the resurrection. Some families choose it for cost, or for distance, or a family spread far apart, and it's allowed.
The Church's own instruction still prefers burial: a body laid in the ground the way Jesus was laid in a tomb, sown in hope.

teach.h: ASHES REST IN A SACRED PLACE.
teach.b: And when there is cremation, it asks that the ashes rest in a sacred place, like a cemetery, rather than being scattered or kept at home, so the dead stay remembered and prayed for.
The instruction's Latin name is worth repeating: Ad resurgendum cum Christo, to rise with Christ. Both sides of the table want what Tobit wanted with a shovel at night: this person mattered.

how: Catholics hold a funeral Mass or a vigil and a committal at the grave; the Church permits cremation but prefers burial, and asks that ashes be laid to rest in a cemetery or other sacred place.

o: pray at a grave once a year
lay the dead to rest with honor
dig graves as a cemetery's job

games.q: the dinner and the grave — tap the pairs.
p: left a feast to bury a stranger
offered Tobit's prayer to the Lord
rest in a sacred place, not scattered

s: it permits it, as long as it isn't chosen to deny the resurrection. it prefers burial.
the Church asks that ashes not be scattered
they're to rest in a sacred place, like a cemetery, so the dead are remembered and prayed for.
Tobit buried the dead only when it was safe
a king condemned him for it. he fled, came back, and did it again.

games.q: say a friend figures cremation is just the practical choice and burial is old habit. state the case for burial at its strongest.
o: a body laid in the ground in hope, like Jesus in the tomb, with a place to remember and pray.
burial is required; Catholics who choose cremation are breaking Church law.
burial is the older custom, and older customs are always the safer choice.
games.why: the Church permits cremation but prefers burial: a body sown in hope of rising, and a grave where the dead are remembered and prayed for.

practice: Find a photo of someone who has died, on your phone or on a shelf, or just write their name down. Look at it for the whole sit, without hurrying past.
If you pray, you can pray for them the way Catholics pray at a graveside; if not, simply let them be remembered.

wordCard.voice: Bury the dead. Lay the dead to rest with honor, and keep them remembered, the way Tobit did in the dark.

orig.note: Latin: to bury, the verb in the traditional Latin list of the works of mercy.

carryVoice: Your line: honor the dead. Both sides of that dinner table want the same thing. Rest well.
